question_stem: Radon-222 $(^{222}_{86}\text{Ra})$ is a radioactive gas that decays randomly with a decay constant of $7.55 \times 10^{-3} \text{hour}^{-1}$.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
The activity of radon gas in a sample of $4.80 \times 10^{-3} \text{m}^3$ of air taken from a building is $0.600 \text{Bq}$.

There are $2.52 \times 10^{25}$ air molecules in a volume of $1.00 \text{m}^3$ of air.

Calculate, for $1.00 \text{m}^3$ of the air, the ratio

$$\frac{\text{number of air molecules}}{\text{number of radon atoms}}.$$
